title: Premium Accounting Basis for a Return of Premium on Released Cover
content:
When a policyholder gives up their own cover under the Travel Protection Plans, the premium returned is the
premium the record shows collected, taken in the proportion of the cover still to run and at the share the terms
of the plan allow.

## The quantities

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| The premium the record shows collected | The whole of the lines charged and the re-ratings raised on the policy, together with the lines already returned on it |
| The days of cover bought | The days of the journey, its first and last both counted |
| The days of cover remaining | The whole of the days of cover bought |
| The proportion of the cover still to run | The days of cover remaining over the days of cover bought |
| The share returned | The plan's free-look share |

The premium returned is never less than nothing and is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end, with no
intermediate figure rounded.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A policy's premium record carries charges of 680.00 and a re-rating of 45.00, with nothing yet returned on it,
so the premium the record shows collected is 725.00. The journey runs from the 10th to the 19th, so the days of
cover bought are 10, and the days of cover remaining are the whole of those 10. The proportion of the cover
still to run is therefore one, and at a free-look share of 100 per cent the premium returned is 725.00.

On the same record with a share of 50 per cent, the premium returned would be 362.50. The figures and dates are
hypothetical.
